topics.title: What is the Gendang Beleq?
topics.summary: The Gendang Beleq is a traditional drum ensemble from the island of Lombok in Indonesia.
facts: The Gendang Beleq is a traditional percussion ensemble of the Sasak people, the main ethnic group of Lombok island in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia.
The ensemble is built around very large drums and is played by a group of musicians who perform together, often in a procession.

lesson.teach: The Gendang Beleq is a traditional drum ensemble. It belongs to the Sasak people, who live on the island of Lombok in Indonesia, just east of Bali.
lesson.question: Which people does the Gendang Beleq belong to, and on which island do they live?
lesson.hint: The people share their name with a word that starts with 'Sa', and their island is east of Bali.
lesson.explain: The Gendang Beleq is the Sasak people's ensemble, from the island of Lombok.

lesson.teach: It is a percussion ensemble, so rhythm is the heart of the music. Many musicians play together, which makes teamwork very important.
lesson.question: In your own words, what kind of music group is the Gendang Beleq?
lesson.hint: Think about what the musicians hit to make sound.

quiz.question: Which province of Indonesia is Lombok part of?
quiz.explain: Lombok is part of West Nusa Tenggara (NTB).

topics.title: What does the name mean?
topics.summary: Gendang Beleq means 'big drum' in the Sasak language.
facts: 'Gendang' means drum, and 'beleq' means big in the Sasak language, so Gendang Beleq means 'big drum'.
The name is also written Gendang Belek.

lesson.teach: The name has two words. 'Gendang' means drum. 'Beleq' means big in the Sasak language.
lesson.question: So what does 'Gendang Beleq' mean in English?
lesson.hint: Gendang is the drum; beleq describes its size.

lesson.teach: You will see the name spelled two ways in books and websites. Both refer to the same ensemble.
lesson.question: Can you tell me the other common spelling of 'Beleq'?
lesson.hint: It ends with a k instead of a q.
lesson.explain: The other spelling is 'Belek', as in Gendang Belek.

quiz.question: What does the word 'beleq' mean?
quiz.hint: It describes the size of the drums.

topics.title: The instruments
topics.summary: Two large drums lead the ensemble, supported by gongs and other percussion.
facts: Two large drums form the heart of the ensemble. They are traditionally described as a male drum, gendang mama, and a female drum, gendang nina.
Other instruments commonly named in the ensemble include gongs, the reyong, the petuk, cymbal-type oncer and sometimes a bamboo flute called suling.

lesson.teach: Two big drums lead the ensemble. By tradition one is called the male drum, gendang mama, and the other the female drum, gendang nina.
lesson.question: What are the two big drums called?
lesson.hint: One name sounds like 'mother' and both end in 'a'. They are gendang mama and gendang ...?
lesson.explain: They are gendang mama (male) and gendang nina (female).

lesson.teach: The drums are joined by other instruments such as gongs, the reyong, the petuk, cymbal-type oncer and sometimes a bamboo flute called suling.
lesson.question: Name one instrument in the ensemble besides the big drums.
lesson.hint: Think of a large metal disc that is struck, or the bamboo flute.
lesson.explain: Gongs, the reyong, petuk, oncer and the suling flute all join the drums.

topics.title: When it is played
topics.summary: It is played at weddings, to welcome guests and at cultural events.
facts: The Gendang Beleq is performed at celebrations such as Sasak weddings, where it can accompany the wedding procession called nyongkolan.
It is also played to welcome honoured guests and at festivals and official cultural events.

lesson.teach: At a Sasak wedding the Gendang Beleq can lead the procession called nyongkolan, the parade that brings the couple and their families through the village.
lesson.question: At what kind of family celebration might the ensemble accompany a procession?
lesson.hint: Think of a celebration where two people get married.
lesson.explain: It accompanies wedding processions called nyongkolan.

lesson.teach: Weddings are not the only time. The ensemble also welcomes honoured guests and performs at festivals and cultural events.
lesson.question: Besides weddings, name another occasion when it is played.
lesson.hint: Think about how a village might greet an important visitor, or a big public celebration.
lesson.explain: It is also played to welcome guests and at festivals and cultural events.

topics.title: History and origins
topics.summary: It was once linked to warriors and kingdoms, and is now mainly cultural.
facts: In its origins the ensemble is linked to the Sasak kingdoms of Lombok, where it was played to accompany warriors going to war.
Over its history it has become mainly a ceremonial and cultural performance rather than a battle tradition.

lesson.teach: In the past the ensemble is linked to the Sasak kingdoms. Its loud, powerful sound was played to accompany warriors going to war.
lesson.question: What was the ensemble traditionally played for in the old kingdoms?
lesson.hint: Think of what soldiers prepare for.
lesson.explain: It accompanied warriors going to war.

lesson.teach: Times have changed. Today the Gendang Beleq is mainly a ceremonial and cultural performance that keeps Sasak heritage alive.
lesson.question: How is the ensemble mostly used today?
lesson.hint: It is no longer for battle. Think of celebrations and heritage.
lesson.explain: Today it is a ceremonial and cultural performance.

topics.title: The players and their costume
topics.summary: Musicians in traditional Sasak dress often play while walking in procession.
facts: Performers wear traditional Sasak dress, including a headcloth, and the ensemble often performs on the move in a procession rather than seated.
Because the musicians usually walk while they play, the large drums are carried on the body.

lesson.teach: The musicians often play while walking together in a procession rather than sitting still. The big drums are carried on the body.
lesson.question: How does the ensemble often perform at a wedding: in what kind of formation?
lesson.hint: They do not stay seated. Think of a moving line of people.
lesson.explain: The players often walk in a procession while they perform.

lesson.teach: The performers dress in traditional Sasak clothing, including a headcloth, which makes the parade colourful and proud.
lesson.question: What do the performers wear?
lesson.hint: Think of the clothes that show their culture.
lesson.explain: They wear traditional Sasak dress, including a headcloth.
